evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 壞: Shuowen entry and graphic history
evidence.text: The entry gives Shuowen’s account, “敗也。从土，褱聲” (“to be ruined; from 土, with 褱 as phonetic”), and records Shuowen’s reduced ancient form 𡎯 and Zhou script form 𣀤. The database reports no oracle-bone examples, but lists bronze and manuscript examples. It cites a Qin bronze inscription for the place-name use “壞德,” read as 褱德, and Warring States Guodian slips for the ordinary sense of being ruined: “聖者不在上，天下必壞.” It also records a Qin Shuihudi legal manuscript use, “所城有壞者.” These show early uses of the graph; the place-name reading and the ruin sense must not be conflated.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「壞」

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, transcribed at Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十三 土部: 壞
evidence.text: Shuowen defines 壞 as 敗 (“ruin, defeat”) and analyzes it as 从土褱聲. The same entry distinguishes a reduced ancient form 𡎯 and a Zhou script form 𣀤. This is an early lexicographic account, not proof by itself of the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字/13 - 維基文庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 褱: form, Shuowen, and attested uses
evidence.text: The entry says bronze 褱 is composed of 衣 and 眔, with 眔 also serving phonetic function in the database’s account; it relates 褱 graphically and lexically to 懷. Shuowen gives 褱 as 俠 and alternatively 橐, and notes uncertainty about 眔 as its phonetic. Bronze and manuscript examples are cited for 褱 used for 怀念/懷 (“remember, cherish”) and related senses. This supports treating 褱 as a separately attested phonetic graph in 壞; the account does not supply a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for standalone 褱.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「褱」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 坏: Shuowen entry and bronze usage
evidence.text: This entry identifies traditional 壞 as the simplified-form counterpart of 坏, while separately describing the historical 坏 graph as 土 plus phonetic 不. It cites bronze inscription evidence for 坏 meaning a mound and quotes the Qin Gong gui phrase “十又二公，才(在)帝之坏,” interpreted as the high mound or mountain where the Qin ancestors are with the deity. No oracle-bone example is shown in its form inventory.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「坏」

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, transcribed at Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十三 土部: 坏
evidence.text: Shuowen defines 坏 as “丘再成者也。一曰：瓦未燒。从土，不聲”: a mound with a second rise; alternatively, an unbaked tile; formed from 土 with 不 as phonetic. This is a historical lexicographic report. Its two glosses alone do not establish the semantic chronology between mound and unbaked pottery.
evidence.title: 說文解字/13 - 維基文庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 坯: relationship with 坏 and early senses
evidence.text: The database describes modern lexical 坯 as 土 plus phonetic 丕, while reporting that Shuowen’s small-seal form is 坏 with 不 phonetic. It cites Erya for 坯 as a one-tier mound and Huainanzi and Qimin yaoshu for 坯 meaning unbaked brick, tile, or pottery. Its examples support early use of the related mound and unbaked-material senses, but do not prove a single semantic path from one to the other.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「坯」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 坏/坯 variant classification and readings
evidence.text: The entry treats 坏 as a variant of 坯 for readings pēi and pī, cites Song-era Guangyun’s definition of 坯 as unbaked tile and later sources on 坏/坯 variant usage, and separately directs readers to 壞 for the huài reading. Thus 坏’s historical lexical readings and its standardized simplified use for 壞 are different functions of the same written form.
evidence.title: 坏 (坯) - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》

evidence.source: State Language Commission, 《簡化字總表》 (1986 edition), transcribed at Wikisource
evidence.field: Simplified/traditional mapping
evidence.text: The published character table lists 坏〔壞〕. Its accompanying notice dates republication of the standard table to 1986-10-10 and says forms in the table are the standard simplified forms. This directly documents modern standardization of 坏 as the simplified form of 壞; it does not mean the older 坏 graph originated as a simplification.
evidence.title: 簡化字總表（1986年版）

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese Reconstruction, version 1.1
evidence.field: 壞 readings and dataset notation
evidence.text: The dataset lists 壞 huài with Middle Chinese hweajH and Old Chinese *N-[k]ˤ<r>uj-s (“be destroyed”); hweajH and *m-[k]ˤ<r>uj-s (“destroy”); hwojX and *N-[k]ˤujʔ (“be destroyed”); hwojX and *m-[k]ˤujʔ (“destroy”); and kweajH with *[k]ʷˤ<r>ujʔ-s (“destroy”). These are distinct listed readings and glosses and should not be collapsed. The local Baxter–Sagart TSV independently matches all five 壞 rows exactly. It has two 不 rows, both pjuw and *pə, with separate glosses (“not” and “writing brush”); it has no standalone 褱 row. No direct B&S comparison between 壞 and 褱 can therefore be made from this dataset. This is a reading comparison limit, not evidence against 褱’s documented phonetic role in the compound.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 不: competing graphic analyses and early uses
evidence.text: The database records two competing analyses of 不’s early graph: plant-root/茇-related and flower-calyx/柎-related. It reports oracle-bone use of 不 as a negative particle as well as names, and multiple bronze uses. The source does not establish that the depicted early object supplies the pronunciation relevant to 坏; the Shuowen account specifically calls 不 the phonetic in 坏.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析: 不

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 壞 pronunciation and Guangyun readings
evidence.text: The page records modern Mandarin huài and two Guangyun fanqie entries, 古壞 and 胡怪, with corresponding Middle Chinese categories 見合二皆去 and 匣合二皆去. These are traditional-form 壞 readings, not evidence for the sound of the ancient object represented by any component.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「壞」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 壞: Shuowen analysis, forms, dated contexts and readings
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Shuowen’s analysis of 壞 as 敗也, 从土褱聲, with reduced ancient form 𡎯 and Zhou form 𣀤. It reports no oracle-bone example, but lists bronze and manuscript forms. A Qin bronze has 壞德 read as the place name 褱德; Warring States Guodian slips use 壞 in the sense “be ruined” (天下必壞), and Shuihudi Qin slips use it in 所城有壞者. The page gives Guangyun fanqie 古壞 and 胡怪. These contexts attest separate uses; the place-name reading is not evidence for the ruin sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「壞」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 坏: graph analysis, bronze use, readings
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes historical 坏, analyzed as 土 plus phonetic 不, from the modern simplified-form correspondence to 壞. It cites bronze evidence for 坏 meaning a mound, including the Qin Gong gui phrase 十又二公，才(在)帝之坏, interpreted as the mound or mountain where Qin ancestors are with the deity. The page reports no oracle-bone example and lists Shuowen’s two glosses: a mound with a second rise, and unbaked tile. The glosses do not by themselves establish which sense came first.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「坏」

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, transcribed at Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十三 土部: 坏 and 壞
evidence.text: The inspected 土部 text gives separate entries: 坏 is 丘再成者也，一曰瓦未燒，从土不聲; 壞 is 敗也，从土褱聲. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of either graph’s original formation or a semantic sequence between their senses.
evidence.title: 說文解字/13 - 維基文庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 褱: Shuowen, form and readings
evidence.text: The entry reports Shuowen’s analysis of 褱 as 从衣眔聲, glossed 俠 and alternatively 橐, with Shuowen’s note that 眔 may not be phonetic and the matter is unclear. Its own account describes bronze and manuscript uses and connects 褱 graphically and lexically with 懷. It supports 褱 as the independently recorded phonetic graph named for 壞, but does not supply a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction for standalone 褱.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「褱」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 坏: modern and traditional mappings
evidence.text: The entry records modern Mandarin huài alongside pī readings and links 坏 and 壞 in its modern simplified/traditional interface. These are distinct functions of the written form; the huài reading should not be projected onto older mound or pottery attestations without contextual evidence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「坏」

evidence.source: 字形演變字源頁，國學大師
evidence.field: 坏: form history and graphic variants
evidence.text: The page labels forms as Warring States, Shuowen seal, Shuowen ancient and Zhou forms, Qin slips, Han silk manuscript and later clerical/regular forms. It says the Qin-slip form is close to seal, with 褱’s 罒 written vertically as 目; some Chu forms show component variation or omission. It also reports 坏 used for 壞 in Yuan-era editions, while distinguishing that usage from the older 坏 variant of 坯. This secondary account provides form descriptions and cited examples, not direct examination of the images here.
evidence.title: 坏字形演变字源_汉字「坏」

evidence.source: 國學大師 page citing bronze catalog entries
evidence.field: 坏: bronze character examples and catalog labels
evidence.text: The inspected page labels three reproduced forms: 競卣, Western Zhou early; 鄂侯鼎, Western Zhou late; 秦公簋, Spring and Autumn middle. Its source labels identify the catalog references as 集成5425, 集成2810 and 集成4315. These are reproductions of recorded character forms, not photographs inspected in this research.
evidence.title: 坏字形演变字源_汉字「坏」
